title: kv: sparse-region reclaimer and spill backpressure control for KV cache
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Context and motivation: The KV cache has been the primary driver of tail latency spikes and memory churn on multi-tenant serving nodes. Previous approaches (compaction, slab segregation, proactive spill) helped but left two recurring issues: 1) fragmentation across sparse collector regions that prevents reclaiming idles without evicting hot keys, and 2) uncontrolled spill-over that floods the disk path and backpressure cascades into request queues. This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: (A) sparse-region reclaimer (SRR) which does fine-grained region-level free-list reclamation and compaction hints, and (B) spill backpressure controller (SBC) that applies adaptive admission control to spill workers and integrates with scheduler kernel-selection to avoid contention with hot inference kernels.

Design summary: (A) SRR splits large KV arenas into sparse regions and maintains a per-region occupancy estimate and fragmentation score; regions with low utilization are reclaimed asynchronously with a conservative eviction budget to avoid removing recently-accessed items. Reclamation prefers cold regions determined by an exponential decay of access counters plus a hotness hysteresis window to reduce oscillation. (B) SBC monitors current disk spill queue length, average spill latency, and tail CPU load. When any signal crosses configured thresholds, SBC throttles new spill tasks by moving them into a timed backoff queue and signals the scheduler to deprioritize maintenance threads in favor of inference kernels. SBC exposes a soft-reservation API so the serving runtime can opt-in to reserve a small protected KV pool for critical routes.

What changed (high level): - Implemented sparse region metadata and reclamation loop in redwood/serving/kv/region_reclaimer.{cc,h} - Added fragmentation scoring and eviction budget controller in redwood/serving/kv/evictor.cc - Introduced spill backpressure controller in redwood/serving/kv/spill_controller.{cc,h} and integrated with the existing spill worker. - Scheduler integration layer: scheduler/hints.cc to accept maintenance hints (deprioritize, throttled) and kernel selection glue that prefers lower-latency kernels when SBC signals high IO contention. - New telemetry: metrics for region_fragmentation_score, srr_reclaims, spill_backpressure_level, spill_throttle_events. - Unit and integration tests under redwood/serving/kv/tests/*, bench harness in benchmark-lab/kv-spillback to reproduce backpressure scenarios.

Example snippet (region reclaim hint):
  // pseudo: mark region for compact if fragmentation_score > threshold && age > min_age
  if (score > cfg.reclaim_fragmentation_threshold && now - region.last_touch > cfg.min_cold_age) {
    reclaim_queue.push(region.id);
  }

Benchmarks: Synthetic mixed workload with 40% large seq generation + 60% short-chat showed: - 95th token latency reduced by ~18% on nodes under memory pressure - Disk spill queue length 6x lower during peaks after SBC engages - No measurable regression (<1%) in median latency for cold-only workloads

Testing and verification: Added deterministic unit tests for region metadata transitions, property-based tests for eviction budget not exceeding configured bounds, and integration test that simulates sustained spill throughput while verifying SBC transitions through green->yellow->red states. Canary rollout: feature flag redwood.kv.srr enabled off by default; enable for 5% of serving nodes for 48 hours with increased telemetry before wider rollouts.

Risk and mitigations: - Risk: Overly aggressive reclamation could evict keys that are about to be used. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, hotness hysteresis, and a canary rollout. - Risk: SBC could starve maintenance leading to long-term fragmentation. Mitigation: SBC uses a weighted-leaky-bucket that always allows a minimum background maintenance budget.

Related work / follow-ups: - Followup planned to add cross-node cooperative eviction hints for Dedicated clusters (ENG-4210). - Next iteration will add async kernel-safe compaction to enable reclaim without stop-the-world pauses.

Rollout and merge notes: Feature gated. CI green after two reruns (flake in perf test). Merged via squash.

review_comments: Jordan Li: Please add a small stress harness that exercises threshold transitions — can we reproduce the yellow->red oscillation?
Ava Martinez: Added harness under benchmark-lab/kv-spillback and an integration test that asserts monotonic backpressure state transitions.
Ravi Patel: We should make the soft-reservation configurable per-tenant. Also ensure scheduler hints have a bounded cost to avoid scheduling thrash.
Ava Martinez: Soft-reservation can be toggled per-route via the API; scheduler hint rate limiting added (max 10 hints/s).
Maya Chen: Verified tests locally and ran the bench profile; observed 15-20% 95th improvement on our CI-sized instance. Approving once CI stabilizes.
release_notes: Add sparse-region reclamation and adaptive spill backpressure to reduce KV cache-induced tail latency and disk spill storms; feature is behind a feature flag and can be gradually enabled per-cluster.
